For F5 (14:17–14:29: 3.64 km driven against 0.77 km of optimal route, +2.87 km, straying up to 1553 m off route) the incident screen fails — no qualifying incident, and speed band alone does not exempt — so RD-4(c) sends this segment back to RD-2 [F5][RD-4][RD-2]. claims.assertion: The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F9 shows a metered breakdown: base $3.90 + distance 9.61 km + time + waiting), so extra kilometres driven enter the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch applies.
The car covered 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%) (F1), taking 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate (F3), and 5.67 km of excess distance was billed at $1.41/km for $7.99 (F6).

Off-route segment 14:10–14:15 drove 2.68 km where the optimal route covers 0.83 km, adding 1.85 km and straying up to 803 m from the optimal route; no rider message before 14:10 described or authorised that diversion.

The rider's only route-related words before departure were 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11, 14:02) — a request for a stop, not consent to a 1,553 m diversion; the driver's 14:01 proposal (F10) named only 'round by Cavenagh', a road the record never ties to either driven segment (no road-name fact, no stop located on Cavenagh Road).

Off-route segment 14:17–14:29 drove 3.64 km where the optimal route covers 0.77 km, adding 2.87 km, reaching 1,553 m from the optimal route — consistent with the driver's own statement that he went to a 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14), a stop the rider never named and was never told about before departure.

The unexcused detour exceeded the agreed stop: the car sat stationary 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 at a point 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off, deep inside segment 14:17–14:29 (F5); on a non-TAXI service no in-trip stop charge is published (G6) — but here the meter's waiting unit was billed at $1.08 (F7).

The driver's 'accident' justification is only partially supported: an Accident at Orchard Road after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed, was reported 13:52 at 0 m from the optimal route (F18) with Orchard Road in band 1 (0–9 km/h) 14:00–14:10 (F15,F19), which can justify the first minutes of the trip only; Bras Basah Road and Bayfront Avenue were flowing at band 4 and band 3 (F16, F17), so no congestion supports driving out to Beach Road and back.

Any portion of the 5.67 km billed excess that is not excused must be refunded at the metered rate ($1.41/km, F6); on my honest reading the excused corridor covers at most the 0.83 km the optimal route itself would have used in 14:10–14:15, leaving at least 2.87 km (segment 14:17–14:29, entirely rider-unauthorised by F5+F14) plus the 1.85 km of segment F4 unexcused.

The driver has 3 disputes in the last 90 days with 1 upheld (F21); if any segment is found unexcused this case makes a repeated route/cancellation violation and supports an account flag under RD-6 (the honoured profile fact is a supplement, not the finding).

weaknesses: Segment F4 (14:10–14:15) partly follows the rider's own 'Sure' (F11) to the driver's Cavenagh proposal (F10): the judge may read that as a general route authorisation, and the traffic facts F18/F15 give the driver a genuine first-leg incident excuse, so a share of this 1.85 km may be held exempt.

The 7-Eleven stop request itself (F11) is a rider-initiated stop, so the stationary 4 min 10 s (F2, F7) and part of the time charge are arguably the rider's own doing — the meter's waiting unit $1.08 is likely to stand under RD-3(c).

The rider never named a road, so no rider-named-road tie helps; and the driver will argue (F14) that the rider agreed verbally to the Beach Road stop — though G11 says a statement-only consent is not consent, the record is silent on whether the rider was told the Beach Road location before the segment began.

Nothing in the record places either driven segment on Cavenagh Road (no route-name fact, no stop co-ordinates on that road), so the judge may find the scope of the F11 'Sure' undetermined and fall back to a partial or no-action result (G13).

claims.assertion: The first off-route segment (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km: F4) is excused as a justified reroute: an LTA DataMall accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed was reported at 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and before the segment began (F18), corroborated by Orchard Road being at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe congestion) during 14:00–14:10 (F15), so under RD-4(a) that segment is no_action.

The rider expressly consented before that segment to the Cavenagh route: the driver asked at 14:01 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) and the rider answered '#2 14:02 Sure' (F11), with the segment starting at 14:10 (F4), so the consent message precedes the segment as RD-5 requires.

The chat also shows the rider raised the stop herself: '#2 14:02 Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) and the driver agreed '#3 14:03 Ok' (F12), so the stop on Beach Road was a stop the rider requested, not a driver's errand, and RD-3 governs it.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) matches the 7-Eleven stop the rider asked for (F11) and the driver's statement that he stopped at the 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14); the record nowhere places the stop anywhere else, and no GPS fact ties the car to Beach Road specifically, so the correspondence between the agreed 7-Eleven and this stop is at best undetermined (G13).

The driver honestly reads the second off-route segment (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km: F5) as not agreed: the rider's only pre-segment message was a request to stop at a 7-Eleven 'on the way' (F11), she never named the place, and the segment ran up to 1553 m off the optimal route (F5), so the rider consented to a short stop, not to this route change — the honest ground for that segment is not an exemption but RD-3(b)/'scope_other'.

On that non-exempted segment the refund is fare-neutral for the platform: only the segment's extra 2.87 km (F5) converts at this trip's metered rate of $1.4100/km (F6), i.e. about $4.05, against the complaint; the driver does not contest a partial refund of that extra distance plus the waiting time attributable to it.

The $1.08 waiting charge (F7) is a RydeTAXI metered waiting unit charge for the 4 min 10 s stop (F2, F7), not a flat fee, and RD-3(c) says RydeTAXI waiting is charged per meter unit and is not refunded.

No safety escalation is warranted: the chat is three ordinary messages with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F10–F13), and the driver's account of a traffic-driven reroute matches the LTA accident record (F14, F18).

A flag_account request under RD-6 is not supported: the driver's 90-day record is 1 upheld dispute and it is a no-show, not a route dispute (route: 0) (F21), so the 'repeated route deviation' precondition is absent.

weaknesses: The overall detour is large and mostly unexplained: actual 9.6 km vs optimal 3.9 km (+5.7 km, +144%, F1) and 26.5 min vs 7.7 min estimated (F3) — the judge will weigh F1/F3 heavily against the driver.

The rider's only pre-segment words were 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11); nothing in F11 or F10 names Beach Road, so the rider will argue (correctly on the record) that agreeing to a stop 'on the way' cannot authorise a 2.87 km / 1553 m detour (F5).

The driver's written statement names the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F14) but no GPS or chat fact places the car on Beach Road or ties F5/F2 to that named road, so under G13 the judge may find the location undetermined rather than accepted as the rider's named stop.

The driver admitted 'I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14) — a store of his own choosing off the optimal route, which invites the rider's RD-3(b) argument that the stop's location was the driver's pick, not the rider's.
The driver's 90-day profile shows prior disputes including 1 upheld (F21), which the rider may use to colour the reroute even though it is a no-show, not a route case.

points.response: The accident (F18) and Orchard Road band 1 at 14:00-14:10 (F15) support at most a reroute onto the parallel trunk road for the first minutes; F4's segment already strays up to 803 m from the optimal route, which is not a bypass of an incident sitting 0 m from that route, so RD-4(a) cannot exempt the whole 1.85 km.

The rider's 'Sure' (F11) answers a proposal naming Cavenagh Road (F10), so RD-5 requires a record tying the segment to that road; no fact places the car on Cavenagh Road or locates the stop there, and the driver's own statement ties his driving to the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F14), so F4 is at most undetermined and cannot be exempted as consent.

F11 asked only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' and named no place; it is the driver who says he chose 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14), so under RD-3(b) the stop's location was the driver's pick and it does not excuse the 2.87 km route change.

I do not rely on the stationary period (F2) to prove a Beach Road location; the stop's duration is handled under RD-3(c) and what is contested is the driven route, which is unexcused as a scope question wherever exactly the car stood (F5).

The driver's own honest reading matches my brief: the rider agreed to a short stop only, so F5's 2.87 km is a route change outside the agreed scope (RD-3(b)); the ground I state for F5 is driver_errand because the driver admits the store was one he knew at Beach Road (F14), a stoppage of his own choosing.

The driver concedes F5 is non-exempt yet prices only 2.87 km; F4's 1.85 km is equally unexcused once the Cavenagh authorisation fails the RD-5 tie test, so the refund is (1.85 + 2.87) km x $1.41/km = $6.66 per F6, and I hold that figure.
Conceded: the $1.08 metered waiting charge (F7) for the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) is a RydeTAXI waiting unit under RD-3(c) and is not sought back; my claim concerns excess mileage only.
Agreed: the three timestamped messages (F10-F13) contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is sought.

Withdrawn as a request: F21 shows the driver's route-upheld count is 0, so RD-6's repeated-route precondition is not met and I no longer ask for flag_account; C9's underlying citation of F21 is not contested.

I keep C8 but restate its arithmetic: only the extra kilometres of the unexcused segments, 1.85 km (F4) + 2.87 km (F5) = 4.72 km, are refundable at this trip's own metered rate of $1.4100/km (F6), i.e. $6.66, because RD-2 refunds extra kilometres of unexcused segments only.
Conceded — the metered branch of RD-2 applies, and the driver does not dispute that only non-exempt extra kilometrage is refundable, which is what D6 already accepts.

The headline figures are correct (F1, F3, F6), but they are aggregates; RD-1/RD-2 decide segment by segment, and the driver's position is that the 1.85 km of the 14:10–14:15 segment is excused by the DataMall accident on the optimal route and the rider's own 'Sure' (F4, F18, F11), leaving only the second segment's 2.87 km to answer for.

A rider message before 14:10 did authorise it: 'Sure' at 14:02 (F11) in answer to the driver's 14:01 route proposal (F10) — the rider's own advocate concedes F18/F15 give this first leg a genuine incident excuse, so this 1.85 km should be held exempt under RD-4(a)/RD-5 (F4).

The rider is right that no record ties the agreed 'Cavenagh' route to either driven segment (no road-name fact, no stop located on Cavenagh Road), so the reach of the general route authority in F11 is undetermined; but the driver's point is only the narrower one that 'Sure' plus the Orchard incident (F18) excuses the first leg, not that the second leg was authorised.

(F11) and the driver agreed (F12) — so the stop is a rider-requested stop under RD-3, not a driver's errand; the driver's statement (F14) names Beach Road but no GPS fact places the car or the stop there, so the location of the stop is undetermined (G13), which is exactly why the driver concedes the second segment rather than defending it.

Conceded in the main: the 4 min 10 s stationary period (F2) sat inside the driver-chosen Beach Road loop (F5), so the extra 2.87 km is conceded via D5/D6; the meter's waiting unit $1.08 (F7) stands under RD-3(c) because the rider requested a stop (F11), and the rider's own weakness list agrees it is likely to stand.

This supports the driver on the first leg: the accident was 0 m from the optimal route and reported at 13:52, before the trip (F18), and Orchard Road was in band 1 (0–9 km/h) 14:00–14:10 (F15), so RD-4(a) excuses the 14:10–14:15 segment; the rider is correct that bands 3–4 on Bras Basah and Bayfront (F16, F17) excuse nothing, which is why the driver concedes the second segment.

The driver accepts the metered arithmetic (F5, F6) and asks the judge not to treat F4's 1.85 km as unexcused, since RD-4(a) applies to that segment (F18, F15); on the refundable amount the driver's figure of about $4.05 (2.87 km × $1.41/km) is materially lower than the rider's $6.66 because the rider's total double-counts the excused first leg.
